# The topology generated by finite rational spectral tests

Author: Worker 36.

For a complete ultrametric normed field `K` and a presented strict affinoid
algebra `P`, this module constructs a topology on the group `Aut P` of actual
bounded `K`-algebra automorphisms. Its identity neighborhoods are generated by
the published finite rational spectral test subgroups. The topology is named
`rationalSpectralTopology P` and is always supplied explicitly in the laws;
the module does not install a global topology instance on `Aut P`.

For a test `t`, write `H(t)` for the subgroup of automorphisms that preserve
`t.domain.locus` setwise and whose induced action on the actual quotient
`t.domain.algebra` moves `t.element` by spectral size at most `t.radius`.
The radius is strictly positive. Spectral size is expressed by a universal
inequality over the Banach spectrum, without choosing a maximum or assuming a
nonempty spectrum. For a finite family `tests`, write `H(tests)` for the
intersection of its `H(t)`; this is the imported
`finiteRationalSpectralSubgroup tests`.

`rationalSpectralBasisSets P` consists exactly of the underlying sets of these
subgroups, initially allowing finite index types in `Type` (universe zero).
The field and quotient sections retain their general universe `u`. This
choice does not discard tests: `finiteRationalSpectralSubgroup_reindex` proves
invariance under an equivalence of finite index types in any two universes,
and `finiteRationalSpectralSubgroup_mem_basis` transports any finite family
along an equivalence with `Fin n`. It follows that finite families from any
index universe give members of this same basis. Empty families are included
and give the whole group.

`rationalSpectralGroupFilterBasis P` constructs all the `GroupFilterBasis`
fields, rather than taking topological-group compatibility as an assumption.
The empty family proves nonemptiness of the basis. Concatenation on a sum of
finite index types gives exactly the intersection of two test subgroups.
Every basis set contains the identity, is closed under multiplication, and is
closed under inversion because it is a subgroup. Finally, for an automorphism
`g`, transport every test by `g⁻¹`. The published transport law identifies
its subgroup with `g⁻¹ * H(tests) * g`. Conjugating its elements by `g`
therefore lands in `H(tests)`, as required by the filter-basis conjugation
axiom. This uses the actual quotient comparison maps behind spectral test
transport, and introduces no common operator-bound assumption.

`rationalSpectralTopology P` is the topology supplied by Mathlib's
`GroupFilterBasis.topology`. The intrinsic theorem
`rationalSpectralTopology_isTopologicalGroup` proves that multiplication and
inversion are continuous for this topology by applying the corresponding
Mathlib construction theorem to the verified basis.

The two exact neighborhood criteria are:

```text
U is a neighborhood of 1  iff  H(tests) ⊆ U for some finite family tests;
U is a neighborhood of g  iff  g * H(tests) ⊆ U for some finite family tests.
```

Here `g * H(tests)` denotes the image under left multiplication, exactly as
in `mem_nhds_rationalSpectralTopology`. These theorems unfold Mathlib's basis
criteria and the existential definition of `rationalSpectralBasisSets`.
`finiteRationalSpectralSubgroup_mem_nhds_one` gives identity-neighborhood
membership for any finite index universe. The theorem
`isOpen_finiteRationalSpectralSubgroup` then uses Mathlib's fact that a
subgroup containing a neighborhood of one is open in a topological group.
It asserts openness only in this explicitly constructed topology.

This is a derived, restricted implementation of the subgroup-topology
construction in Berkovich's unfinished *Etale equivariant sheaves on p-adic
analytic spaces* (1995–1996), section 1.1, printed/PDF pp. 1–2. That passage
uses finite families of compact analytic domains, analytic functions and
positive tolerances, with non-strict spectral inequalities and setwise domain
preservation; it asserts the topological-group property on p. 2. The present
proof obtains the restricted property from constructed rational tests and
their conjugation law through Mathlib's `Topology/Algebra/FilterBasis.lean`.
It does not import the source's topological-group assertion as an axiom.
The underlying strict affinoid quotients, bounded maps and rational quotient
algebras follow Berkovich's *Non-archimedean analytic spaces*, Trieste lectures
(2009), section 2.1 and Definition 2.1.2 on p. 7, Definition 2.1.11 on p. 8,
and Definition 2.2.1 and Exercise 2.2.2(ii) on p. 9, via the imported Library
constructions.

The scope remains fixed-field automorphisms and the Library's unit-radius
rational presentations. There is no assertion of equality with the full
analytic automorphism topology using all compact analytic domains, or with
a pointwise quotient-norm topology. No Hausdorff or separation property is
asserted. No continuity of the action on spectrum points or quotient sections,
no openness in a different topology, and no structure sheaf or equivariant
site is proved here. The existing section-action convention is forward on
algebras and inverse pullback on spectrum points; inversion invariance of the
test subgroups reconciles the opposite pullback convention in the source.
The hypotheses do not exclude trivial valuations, nilpotents, zero quotients,
empty rational loci or empty test families.
